title: westron component contract
description: One neutral contract per component, spec/components/<id>/<id>.spec.yaml, written in YAML (decisions/0004). Every platform implementation is generated from it and checked against it. `tools/westron spec check` validates a contract against this schema, then applies the rules a schema cannot express: the file name matches the id; no unquoted YAML 1.1 boolean word other than true and false; option values are unique and a default is one of them; no value, state or form is a word Swift cannot use as a case (init, self, none) and no option one it cannot use as an argument label (inout, var, let); no value is the name of a system style of the base control, which westron's overload would shadow (decisions/0003); the Apple strategy fits its base, a style on a control with a style modifier and an extension on one without; an option of type tokens names a group of tokens/ whose tokens are semantic, exist in every mode and are of one type, its default is one of them, and no constraint, case, binding by value, restriction or systemOptions names it; no constraint, case, restriction or systemOptions names an option of type icons; constraints, token bindings, platform restrictions and accessibility states name only options, values and states that exist; no option is named `state`; a binding by value gives every value of its option a token; every case of a binding is reachable, not covered by earlier cases alone or together, and so is its `token`, which cases that match every combination leave unused; a fallback maps each value a platform drops to a value it keeps, and on Apple every value reaches, through Apple's fallback and then the OS's, a value each OS offers; a platform's systemOptions name options that exist and are not restricted; every bound token exists in tokens/ and is not a primitive; a part's `shape` binds a shape, `capsule`, alone or as the token of each of its cases, and nothing else binds one; a component whose accessibility role is none has no intents, keyboard intents or announced states, and no required label; a hiddenLabel needs a required label, the slot label and, on Apple, a style on a base whose initializer with no label view the conventions derive; a case's `state: { all: [...] }` names two or more declared states, and a binding with such a case is checked by enumerating every set of the states its cases name; in a contract with `forms`, each form enters declared states, every declared state is entered by some form, each form's accessibility, the contract's with the form's fields in their place, follows the rules of accessibility, each platform with a strategy names in `bases` a base for every form and no other and names no `base`, and on Apple each form's base is checked as `base` is and the strategy is a style on system controls, or an own component of form view, which names no bases; `bases` belongs only to a contract with forms; an integer option's default is at least its minimum, and constraints, cases, restrictions and systemOptions name no integer option; a mark's enum parameter has unique values and a default among them, and its names are usable in Swift. Lists of names are checked for repeats there too, with a message that names the repeat.

id.description: The component's name in every platform's terms: lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as `button` or `list-row`. The contract lives in spec/components/<id>/<id>.spec.yaml. No prefix (decisions/0003).

status.description: draft: written, not approved; approved: the human approved it and platforms may implement it (decisions/0005); stable: released; deprecated: on its way out.

description.description: What the component is for, in a sentence or two.

consumers.description: The product screens that need the component, as <product>/<screen>, such as `todo-app/list-screen` (decisions/0006). A component without a consumer is not created (AGENTS.md, rule 6).

options.description: What a product chooses, by option name: an enum with its values and, unless every use must name a value, its default; a bool with its default; tokens, whose values are the tokens under one token group, read from tokens/ rather than listed; or icons, whose values are the names of the icon registry, spec/icons/icons.yaml, read from it rather than listed. The names and values become generated names on every platform (AGENTS.md, rule 4).

slots.description: The content a product puts into the component, such as `label` or `icon`.

states.description: Every state the component can be in, such as `hover`, `focus`, `pressed`, `disabled`, `loading`. A platform that never enters some of them says so in `platforms`.

forms.description: The forms of a component that the product picks by the system control it writes, each the same look on its own base control (Chip: selectable on a toggle, pressable on a button, static on a label), by form name: the states it enters, a subset of `states`, and what it announces, where that differs from `accessibility`. A contract with forms names a base per form on each platform, `bases`, in place of `base`, except a platform where it is an own component: there each form is an initializer of its own view, a form a person acts on (its intents hold activate) taking the action (ListRow: with an action and without). Not to be confused with `platforms.apple.form`, the shape of an own component's API.

marks.description: Marks drawn around an instance that are no state of it, by mark name, each with its parameters (ListRow's insertion: the edge and the level a dragged row would land at).

context.description: Settings a product makes once on an ancestor for every instance below it, and for the components the contract says read them, by name, which no option of one instance can carry because they concern the instances together (Disclosure's alignsLeaves: every row of a tree keeps the chevron's cell, empty on a leaf, so trailing content stands in columns). Each is a bool, off where it is not set. On Apple it is the modifier `.<component><Name>(_: Bool = true)`, set through the environment and cascading (spec/conventions.md, "Context a component sets").

constraints.description: Rules between options: when the options have the values in `when`, they must have the values in `require`. A rule on a slot names it in `when` under the key `slots` instead of options: when an instance fills that slot, the options must have the values in `require`, one value each, with severity error (Rule: a labelled rule is a horizontal separator).

tokens.description: Token bindings, by `<part>.<property>` of the component's anatomy, such as `container.background`: one token path; a map from the values of one enum option to token paths; or cases, `{token, cases: [{when, token}]}`, for bindings that depend on several options or on a state.

platforms.description: How each platform implements the contract, and every way it differs from it. A difference between platforms that is not recorded here is a bug (AGENTS.md, rule 5).

name.description: A name that becomes an identifier on every platform: lowerCamelCase ASCII, a lowercase letter first.

tokenPath.description: The dotted path of a token in tokens/, without braces: `color.background.accent`.

integerOption.description: A whole number, such as a row's nesting level: a quantity, not a choice. `default` is required; `minimum`, when given, is the least value, and the default is at least it. The snapshot matrix draws its default and makes it no axis; constraints, cases, bindings by value, platform restrictions and systemOptions do not name such an option yet.

contextSetting.description: One setting of the context: a bool, off where no ancestor sets it, and what it does.

mark.description: Something drawn around an instance that is no state of it, set per instance with its parameters, such as where a dragged row would land. Its first parameter is an enum: where the mark stands, an instance with none drawing no mark; the others are enum, bool or integer parameters with defaults. On Apple it is the modifier `.<mark>Mark(_:…)` (spec/conventions.md, "Marks").

enumOption.description: One value of a closed list; `default`, when given, is one of `values`. An enum option without a default has to be named in every use: a call that leaves it out does not compile, as a SwiftUI variant (spec/conventions.md).

tokenOption.description: One token of a token group: the values are the paths of the tokens under `group`, after the group, such as `heading.large` for `typography.heading.large`. The contract does not list them, so the option and the tokens cannot drift: spec check reads them from tokens/. Every token under the group exists in every mode, is semantic and has one type. `default`, when given, is one of the values; without it, every use names one. Constraints, cases, bindings by value and platform restrictions do not name such an option yet, and it is never a system option.

group.description: The token group, as a dotted path without braces: `typography`, `color.text`.

default.description: A token's path after the group: `body.regular`.

iconOption.description: One icon of westron's icon registry, spec/icons/icons.yaml: the values are the registry's names, in its order, such as `tray` or `chevron`. The contract does not list them, so the option and the registry cannot drift; `tools/westron icons check` validates the registry. It has no default: every use names its glyph (the registry's own `default` is what draws for a name a version does not know, not what a use without a name draws), unless it is `optional`: then a use may name none, and no glyph is drawn. Constraints, cases and platform restrictions do not name such an option yet, and it is never a system option.

optional.description: true: a use may name no glyph, and then none is drawn, such as the glyph at a text field's start (spec/components/text-field). Allowed only where the conventions derive it, an option of a style on a system control; an own view's glyph is always named. An optional option is no axis of the snapshot matrix, which draws it absent: hand-written supplements draw the glyphs (spec/conventions.md).

tokenGroupPath.description: A dotted path in tokens/ of one name or more, without braces.

optionValues.description: Values by option name: one value or a list of them; a bool option takes true or false.

optionValue.description: One value, a list of values, or true or false.

caseConditions.description: A case's when: values by option name, and under `state` one state, a list of states (any of them), or every one of a list at once (`all`).

when.description: Values by option name; or, under the key `slots`, the slots an instance fills, from `slots`, and no option.

severity.description: error: the combination is not allowed; warning: allowed, but advised against.

tokenBinding.description: A token path; a map from the values of one enum option to token paths; or, when the object has `cases`, a case binding. A part's `shape`, such as `container.shape`, binds a shape instead of a token: `capsule`, the platform's own capsule, fully round ends at any height, which no radius draws (design-language/04); in a case binding, each case's token is a shape.

caseBinding.description: The first case whose `when` matches gives the token; when none matches, `token` does, and without `token` the part has no value. A case's `token: null` means the part has no value in that case.

when.description: Values by option name, as in a constraint; the key `state` names one state or a list of states from `states`, and matches when the component is in any of them, or `{all: [...]}`, two states or more, and matches when it is in every one of them at once. A case matches when every key matches.

token.description: A token path, or in the cases of a part's `shape` a shape, `capsule`; null: the part has no value in this case.

accessibility.description: Accessibility in abstract terms; each platform maps them to its own API.

role.description: The abstract role, such as `button`, `checkbox`, `slider`; `none` when the component adds no role of its own (ARIA's `none`): assistive technology reads its content, if it has any, as if the component were not there, and it takes no intents, keyboard intents or announced states, and no required label.

intents.description: What an assistive technology can do with the component, such as `activate` or `dismiss`.

keyboardIntents.description: What the keyboard can do with the component, such as `activate`. A platform or an Apple OS adds its own in `platforms`.

label.description: required: every instance has an accessible label, even when none is visible (an icon-only presentation); optional: it may have none.

hiddenLabel.description: true: an instance may draw no label, its label then given as its accessible name alone where the instance is created, as a required argument, as a check beside a separate title (an empty name still compiles, as an empty label does). It needs `label: required` and the slot `label`. On Apple the conventions derive the initializer of the base control that takes no label view and requires the name (spec/conventions.md, "A label that is not drawn"). Absent or false: a label that is shown is the only way to give it.

states.description: By state from `states`, the abstract state assistive technology announces in it, such as `loading: busy` or `disabled: disabled`.

componentForm.description: One form of a component (`forms`): the states it enters, and what it announces where that differs from the contract's `accessibility`.

states.description: The states this form enters: a subset of `states`, empty for a form that enters none.

formAccessibility.description: What one form announces where it differs from the contract's `accessibility`: each field it names replaces the contract's field of that name for this form, and the rules of `accessibility` hold for the result.

bases.description: In a contract with forms, the base control of each form on this platform, by form name, in place of `base`: `selectable: SwiftUI.Toggle`.

restrictedOptions.description: By enum option, the values a platform offers: a subset of the option's values. An option not named here is offered whole.

restrictedStates.description: The states a platform enters: a subset of `states`. Without it, the platform enters every state.

fallback.description: By restricted option, what a value the platform drops becomes there: one kept value for every dropped one, or a map from each dropped value to a kept one. On Apple every dropped value needs one, since the OSes share one generated enum.

systemOptions.description: Options that are the platform's own API: by option name, the system type or member that carries it, such as `role: SwiftUI.ButtonRole`. The generators make no type for such an option and give the style overload no argument for it: a product sets it on the system control (`Button(role: .destructive)`), and the style reads it there; on an own component it is the system's environment modifier, which the product writes on the component and the system views inside it read (Icon's `scale: SwiftUI.Image.Scale`, `.imageScale(_:)`) (spec/conventions.md).

platformKeyboardIntents.description: Keyboard intents this platform adds to `accessibility.keyboardIntents`, such as `defaultAction` and `cancelAction` on macOS.

reason.description: Why the platform differs from the contract.

appleTarget.description: What one Apple OS keeps of the contract, beyond what all of Apple keeps; or, with `status: unavailable`, that the component does not exist on that OS, since its system control does not (SwiftUI has no DisclosureGroup on watchOS): nothing of it is generated or compiled there, and the description says why. At least one Apple OS keeps it (spec check).

planned.description: Not designed for this platform yet.

strategy.description: style-on-system-control: westron styles the platform's own control, named in `base` (decisions/0003); extension-on-system-control: the platform's own control or view, named in `base`, takes no style, so westron adds extensions to it, such as a modifier, and no type of its own (decisions/0003, point 1); own-component: the platform has no such control, so westron builds one.

base.description: The system control or view, as the platform names it: `SwiftUI.Button`, `SwiftUI.Text`, `GtkButton`, `button` (an HTML element).

baseRequirement.description: A style or an extension goes on a system control, so those strategies name its base, or, in a contract with forms, a base per form in `bases` (spec check rejects both, and `bases` in a contract without forms); an own component has none.

appleForm.description: The shape of an own component's API on Apple (spec/conventions.md, "Own components"): modifier, a modifier on View named after the component, for one that draws around the content it is given and lays nothing out (`.surface(.raised)`); view, a View type named after the component, for one that is a view of its own (`Rule()`).

formRequirement.description: An own component on Apple names the shape of its API in `form`, which the generator and the API parity lint derive the API from; a style or an extension has its shape from its base and names none.

platform.description: A platform: planned, or its strategy with its restrictions.

applePlatform.description: Apple: planned, or its strategy with its restrictions for all of Apple and for each OS.
